newsitem.title: USA: Continental executives unload shares - WSJ.
newsitem.headline: Continental executives unload shares - WSJ.

text.p: Ten high-ranking Continental Airlines officials, including Chief Executive Gordon Bethune, unloaded 1.16 million shares valued at more than $30.3 million in recent weeks, The Wall Street Journal reported Wednesday.
Delta Air Lines is said to be in talks about the possible acquisition of Continental, according to the Journal's story.
It's unclear why the executives would sell during the negotiations, which began in the late summer, the newspaper said.
Most of the sales took place during November, the newspaper said.

The story quoted Bob Gabele, president of CDA Investnet, a Fort Lauderdale, Fla., research firm, saying the sales represented "by far the largest cluster of selling" at Continental since the company emerged from Chapter 11 protection from creditors in April 1993.
